purpose: Cross-field semantic negative and positive controls for the apparel engineering digital thread. These are expected outcomes for a future semantic validator; the current JSON Schema validates structure only.

cases.mutation: Change design.revision from A to B while leaving a fit/drape/3D geometry projection bound to pattern revision A.
cases.invariant: A projection bound to revision A cannot support a claim about revision B without a qualified revalidation receipt.

cases.mutation: Set a BOM item material_id to a value absent from the canonical materials list.
cases.invariant: Every BOM material reference resolves to an exact source identity.

cases.mutation: Duplicate a pattern piece_id while preserving both records.
cases.invariant: Pattern piece identity is unique within a declared pattern revision.

cases.mutation: Mark a physical test as measured while result or evidence_ref is null/empty.
cases.invariant: A measured test result requires an actual result and a resolvable evidence artifact.

cases.mutation: Support a physical drape or fit claim using only a geometry projection whose evidence_class is model_output.
cases.invariant: Simulation or model output cannot establish an independent physical test claim.

cases.mutation: Use one prototype article with article_scope single_prototype to assert capability across production batches and sizes.
cases.invariant: One accepted prototype does not qualify every size, batch, machine or production shift.

cases.mutation: Replace the fabric lot while retaining test evidence bound to the previous lot without applicability review.
cases.invariant: A material-lot substitution triggers dependency analysis and invalidates only the affected claims until reviewed.

cases.mutation: Keep composition_state unknown but emit a supported claim that fibre blend is independently measured.
cases.invariant: Unknown composition cannot be converted into a measured fibre identity.

cases.mutation: Use a TexSortML-style visual class such as jacket or shirt as evidence that the item is cotton, polyester or a specific blend.
cases.invariant: Visual garment-family classification is not fibre-composition evidence.

cases.mutation: Claim fibre-to-fibre recovery or qualified secondary material without an output lot, custody/transfer evidence, mass attribution and output-grade evidence.
cases.invariant: A reported recovery event is not proof of a physically qualified secondary-material output.

cases.mutation: Admit a spectral composition estimate from an instrument whose calibration profile was expired or changed after acquisition.
cases.invariant: A sensor result outside its qualified calibration/currentness envelope must abstain, not silently pass.

cases.mutation: Allocate the same physical material lot quantity to two products or recovery pathways beyond the available measured quantity.
cases.invariant: Physical lot identity and quantity cannot be double-counted across BOM, inventory, reuse and recovery.

cases.mutation: Convert geometry or mass units between source and projection without an explicit conversion rule, source unit and preserved precision/uncertainty.
cases.invariant: Unit conversion must be explicit, reproducible and bounded by declared precision and uncertainty.

cases.mutation: Use a synthetic fixture or simulated run as evidence for a physical material test, article inspection or factory execution claim.
cases.invariant: Synthetic/model evidence cannot be promoted into physical observation or production execution evidence.

cases.mutation: Include restricted supplier, process or lot evidence in a public passport projection without an explicit disclosure grant.
cases.invariant: Evidence availability to the local system does not imply permission to disclose it.

cases.mutation: Record a repair or replacement of a load-bearing/seam-critical component while leaving dependent inspection/test claims current without impact analysis.
cases.invariant: A repair is a lifecycle event; dependent engineering evidence must be evaluated for applicability.

cases.mutation: Bind one manufactured article to an exact design revision, material lots, process events, measured inspections and physical-test artifacts, with no broader batch claim.
cases.invariant: A single article may be qualified for its tested configuration and conditions without extrapolation.

cases.mutation: A spectral sensor reports an out-of-domain or expired-calibration condition and the system marks composition unknown and requests an admissible remeasurement.
cases.invariant: Correct abstention is a valid outcome and is preferable to an unsupported composition assertion.

cases.mutation: A candidate fabric architecture lies outside the calibrated construction/material domain, but the surrogate emits a supported property claim without uncertainty or abstention.
cases.invariant: An inverse-design model must abstain or request a new physical experiment outside its validated domain.

cases.mutation: A surrogate-predicted tensile/drape/thermal value is recorded as an independent physical measurement.
cases.invariant: Predictions can rank candidates; they cannot become measured properties.

cases.mutation: An inverse-designed weave/yarn structure is released for production although the target loom/knitting/finishing capability and process envelope are unknown.
cases.invariant: A property-optimal material candidate is not releasable unless a declared manufacturing route can produce it within its process limits.

cases.mutation: An optimization pipeline picks one candidate using predicted mean only and hides uncertainty, hard-constraint risk and Pareto trade-offs.
cases.invariant: A scalar weighted objective cannot compensate for unresolved hard gates or conceal a candidate's uncertainty.

cases.mutation: Spectra, pixels, physical replicates or frames from the same physical specimen/garment are split across training and held-out evaluation.
cases.invariant: Splits must be grouped by physical specimen/garment and, where possible, source lot/material family.

cases.mutation: A visual category such as jacket/shirt or silhouette is used to support a fibre composition claim.
cases.invariant: Visual garment-family evidence and spectral/material-composition evidence are separate claim types.

cases.mutation: A design is labelled suitable for a recycling route using a sorting-rule profile for a different sensor, plant or process route.
cases.invariant: Sortability is route-, sensor-, calibration- and plant-specific, not a universal product property.

cases.mutation: The BOM omits a membrane, coating, lining, adhesive or low-share component present in the physical garment while the product is marked composition-complete.
cases.invariant: Surface appearance or a main-shell label cannot stand in for complete component-level material identity.

cases.mutation: A product passes design-for-disassembly although the declared separation operation damages the recovered textile or makes it fail its secondary functional profile.
cases.invariant: A separable component is not a successful recovery output unless damage and downstream function are assessed.

cases.mutation: A generic composition rule declares a garment recyclable even though no named downstream plant/process accepts its actual material blend, finish and component mix.
cases.invariant: A rule-level compatibility result must bind to a declared downstream process route and its actual acceptance envelope.

cases.mutation: An inverse-design surrogate detects an out-of-domain candidate, marks the property unresolved and selects a physical coupon test that can reduce the relevant uncertainty.
cases.invariant: Abstention plus informative physical experiment selection is a successful model outcome.

cases.mutation: A garment design satisfies a versioned, sensor- and plant-specific sorting/disassembly profile, with all components, detection limits, join methods and downstream output acceptance explicitly bound.
cases.invariant: A route-scoped compatibility assessment may pass without asserting universal recyclability or environmental benefit.

claim_ceiling: Synthetic semantic test intentions only. No validator implementation, physical testing, dataset evaluation or product qualification is implied.
